title: The winter Mediterranean
subtitle: Not a worse voyage — a different one, and almost nobody is offered it properly.

text: In winter the Mediterranean stops being a beach and becomes a library.
sub: The sea is not the point any more. The shore is — and the shore in January has its own inhabitants back.

items.head: The fleet has largely gone
items.body: Most ships redeploy to warmer water. What remains is a shorter, more deliberate list of sailings.

items.head: Cities replace islands
items.body: Rome, Barcelona, Valletta, Cadiz. Great ports rather than swimming stops, and they hold up in the rain.

items.head: The days are short
items.body: Less usable daylight ashore. An eight-hour call in December is not the eight hours of a June call.

items.head: Weather is a real variable
items.body: Rain and swell are genuine possibilities. Alongside berths matter more here than at any other time.

quote: Winter is the wrong answer if you came for the sea. It is the right one if you came for the shore.

text: Choose the season that matches what you came to do.
sub: Swimming and walking are different holidays wearing the same brochure. Winter simply removes the pretence that a voyage must be about the water.

title: DM me the word WINTER
body: I'll tell you what is genuinely still sailing the Mediterranean in January, and which of it is worth your fortnight.
